latency_case_ms.scope: runner wall time from before the first question through case completion; includes forwards/evaluation, per-call footprint+swap sampling, cache cleanup/GC, and incremental artifact writes; excludes model load

latency_per_case_ms.scope: one remote API request containing all three questions; includes remote service and network effects

jev_latest_separate_remote_system.freeze_note: Reported metrics were regenerated after raw outputs were frozen, following an initial premature scoring pass; no inference was repeated and no tuning was performed.

comparison_caveats: The six local frozen-system results are preserved unchanged in comparison-core-six.json.

Laya and JEV score-label accuracies are comparable on the exact same case IDs and fixture hash; their expected-value and ordinal score MAEs are not supplied because the systems do not expose a comparable common quantity.
Laya case latency is guarded-runner wall time including guard subprocesses, cleanup, and persistence, while other scopes differ; timings are not normalized or used to claim a speed ranking.
LoRA inputs reached 375 tokens versus an observed training maximum of 266; configured training guard was 288 and inference cap was 512, with no truncation recorded.
Results do not support claiming LoRA improvement: the two LoRA systems scored 0/60 all-three correct; Laya scored 1/60.
